# KriolLang Documentation

> KriolLang (Kriol) is a statically-typed, compiled programming language that uses Cape Verdean Creole keywords.

## Overview

KriolLang is designed to make programming accessible to Cape Verdean Creole speakers. It compiles to native code via LLVM/C and features static typing, functions, arrays, strings, and control flow structures.

## Key Information

- Language: Cape Verdean Creole-based programming language
- Paradigm: Imperative, procedural
- Typing: Static
- Compilation: Native code via LLVM/C
- File extensions: .kriol (preferred), .kr
- License: MIT
- Platforms: Linux and Windows, x86_64 (macOS support planned)
- Repository: https://github.com/kriol-lang/kriol

## Installation

Linux:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://kriol.dev/install.sh | sh -s -- --pre
export PATH="$HOME/.kriol:$PATH"
```

Windows (PowerShell; installs kriol.exe and ld.lld.exe, programs run on Windows 7+):

```powershell
& ([scriptblock]::Create((irm https://kriol.dev/install.ps1))) -Pre
```

## Basic Syntax

Entry point function (it takes no parameters and declares no return type):
```kriol
fn inisiu() {
    mostran("Kualeh, Mundu!");
}
```

Comments: `// to end of line` and `/* across lines */` (they do not nest).

Identifiers: variables, functions, parameters and fields start with a lowercase letter or `_`; molda type names start with an uppercase letter.

Top-level variables: a declaration outside any function is visible to the functions declared after it, and any of them can assign to it.

## Data Types

- int: 64-bit signed integer (int64_t); i8..i64, u8..u64, isize, usize are also available
- num: 64-bit floating-point number (double, same as f64); f32 is also available
- bool: boolean (sin = true, nau = false)
- textu: string (char*)

## Keywords and Constructs

- fn: function declaration
- si/sinon: if/else
- nkuantu: while loop
- pa: for loop, `pa int i = 0; i < 10; i += 1 { }`; the step is optional (`pa int i = 0; i < 10 { }`)
- divolvi: return
- mostra/mostran: print without/with newline; both take any number of arguments, written one after another with no separator, and `mostran()` with none prints an empty line
- toma: read one line from stdin as textu; it stops the program if the input ends, unless handled: `tenta toma()` in a function declared `: Erru`, or `toma() sinon "default"`
- kebra: break
- kontinua: continue; both kebra and kontinua affect only the innermost loop
- sai: exit; `sai()` without an argument exits with code 0
- konfirma: assert, with an optional message: konfirma(cond, "message")
- paniku: abort the program with a message: paniku("message")
- molda: struct; literal `Pessoa{nomi = "Ana", idadi = 30}`, fields read and written with `.`
- Recoverable errors: `fn f() int : Erru`, `lansa Erru{mensage = "..."};`, `tenta f()` (propagate), `f() sinon value` (default). An unhandled error stops the program at the call, with a warning at compile time; `kriol --strict` turns warnings into errors

## Documentation Structure

/introducao/sobre - About the language, origin, goals
/introducao/primeiros-passos - Installation and first program
/linguagem/tipos - Data types (int, num, bool, textu)
/linguagem/variaveis - Variable declaration and scope
/linguagem/operadores - Arithmetic, logical, relational operators
/linguagem/controlo-de-fluxo - Conditionals and loops
/linguagem/funcoes - Function declaration and recursion
/linguagem/arrays - Fixed-size and multi-dimensional arrays
/linguagem/strings - Strings and f-string interpolation
/linguagem/estruturas - Structs (molda) - in development
/linguagem/entrada - Input (toma)
/linguagem/conversao-de-tipos - Type conversion
/referencia/vocabulario - Keyword mapping
/referencia/especificacao - Formal specification

## Features

Currently supported:
- Typed variables (int, num, bool, textu, i8..u64, f32, f64, isize, usize)
- Top-level variables shared by every function declared after them
- Functions with return types, recursion and mutual recursion
- Control flow (si/sinon, nkuantu, pa)
- Arrays (fixed size, multi-dimensional, passed and returned by value)
- String interpolation (f-strings)
- Structures (molda): fields, literals, `.` access, value semantics
- Recoverable errors (Erru, lansa, tenta, sinon) and text-to-number conversion
- Input/output (mostra, mostran, toma)
- Native targets (Linux, Windows) and wasm32-wasi

In development:
- macOS support
- Methods and type-associated functions (fazi, Type::function(), value.method())
- Explicit references (ref)
- Modules and imports (inpristan)
- Variable-size collections
- C interoperability
- Standard library, including text functions and file handling

## Example Programs

Hello World:
```kriol
fn inisiu() {
    mostran("Kualeh, Mundu!");
}
```

Fibonacci:
```kriol
fn fibo(int n) int {
    konfirma(n >= 0);
    si n <= 1 {
        divolvi 1;
    } sinon {
        divolvi fibo(n - 1) + fibo(n - 2);
    }
}

fn inisiu() {
    int[10] seq = [0; 10];
    pa int i = 0; i < 10; i += 1 {
        seq[i] = fibo(i);
    }
    mostran(f"Fibonacci: {seq}");
}
```

## Type System

- Static typing with compile-time checks
- Implicit widening: int to num (automatic); as in C, a real stored into an integer is truncated toward zero (`int n = 3.9;` is 3, saturating out of range)
- Explicit casting with C-style syntax: `(int) 3.9`, `(u8) 300`, `(bool) n`; only numbers and bool convert (text is not convertible)
- Typed array literal: `(int[]) [1, 2, 3]`
- Text to number: `textu t = tenta toma(); int n = tenta int::konverti(t);`, `num::konverti(s) sinon 0.0`, also `bool::konverti`; it fails with an Erru on invalid text
- No null types and no uninitialized variables (every declaration has an initial value)
- Division as in C: two integers divide as integers (`7 / 2` is 3), a real operand makes it real; `x op= v` computes in the common type and stores into x's type
- Division or remainder by zero stops the program, for integers and reals
- `!`, `&&` and `||` accept numbers, which are true when not zero, and `&&`/`||` short-circuit
- Integer overflow wraps silently, as in C; only division or remainder by zero (and signed MIN / -1) stops the program
- textu has no operations yet: no `+` to concatenate, no `==` to compare, no indexing, no length; join text with an f-string, `f"{a}{b}"`
- Integer literals adapt to the target type when the value fits; the largest writable integer literal is 9223372036854775807
- Float literals need digits on both sides of the point and have no exponent form; `tipo::konverti("1e3")` does accept exponents
- No `++`, `--`, `<<`, `>>` or ternary `? :`; no switch/case/match and no do-while
- Values are printed with %g for reals (`2.0` prints `2`), `sin`/`nau` for bool, and `[1, 2, 3]` for arrays
- An unhandled error from a function you declared `: Erru` warns at compile time; the builtins `toma` and `tipo::konverti` never warn, not even with --strict
- Arrays and molda are values: assigning, passing and returning copy them; `int[2][3]` has 2 rows of 3 (outermost dimension first)
- Bitwise operators on integers: `&`, `|`, `^`, `~` (and `&=`, `|=`, `^=`); they bind tighter than comparisons

## Limits

- Expression depth: 256 levels (a chain like 1 + 1 + ... counts one level per operator)
- Elements per array dimension: 1,048,576
- Local variables, parameters and returned values: 1 MiB each (declare larger values at the top level)
- Compiled programs get an 8 MiB stack on Linux, Windows and WebAssembly

## Compilation

Compile: `kriol file.kr -o output` (without -o the result is ./a.out)
Optimization: `--opt-lvl <n>`, 0 to 3 (default 2)
Run: `./output`
Compile a snippet with no file: `kriol --text 'fn inisiu() { mostran(1); }'`
WebAssembly: `kriol file.kr --target wasm32-wasi -o file.wasm` (this is what the playground runs)
Emit IR: `kriol file.kr --emit-ir`
Warnings as errors: `kriol --strict file.kr`
Other extensions: `--ignore-extension`
Runtime errors are reported as `file.kr:LINE: erro de execução: message` and exit with code 1; compiler diagnostics are in Portuguese
